Lecture 3: What a reservoir does

A reservoir stores water in wet months and releases it in dry ones. This lecture follows one reservoir through a whole year.

The Kell Reservoir was formed by damming the Varrow River at Kell Gorge.

The Kell Reservoir supplies drinking water to the town of Edrin.

Lecture 3: Capacity

Capacity figures are quoted at full supply level, the highest level the dam is designed to hold in normal operation.

The Kell Reservoir holds 41.6 million cubic metres at full supply.

At full supply the surface of the Kell Reservoir covers 6.3 square kilometres.

Below full supply the reservoir shrinks quickly, because its banks are shallow.

Lecture 3: The Orrin Dam

The Orrin Dam is an earth-fill dam 52 metres high.

Earth-fill dams are cheap to build where clay is plentiful, but they must never be overtopped.

The Orrin Dam's spillway can pass 1,900 cubic metres per second.

Lecture 3: Sediment

Sediment settles where a river slows down, so the upstream arm of a reservoir fills first.

The Kell Reservoir loses about 0.4 percent of its storage to sediment each year.

Most sediment enters the Kell Reservoir from the Tamsk Creek tributary.
